Mutoscope

Privacy Policy

Effective November 17, 2026.

Mutoscope is an Apple TV app for watching the media on your own Plex Media Servers. It works with Plex but is an independent app: it isn't made, endorsed or supported by Plex. Plex and Plex Media Server are trademarks of Plex and used under a license. This policy says what Mutoscope does with information about you. The app shows it in Settings → About → Privacy Policy.

The short version

Mutoscope has no accounts of its own, no ads, no analytics and no tracking. It talks to Plex and to the services you turn on, and it sends the developer nothing unless you report a review or comment. Test versions (TestFlight) can also keep a diagnostics log, only if you allow it, and send it when you choose.

Plex

You sign in with your Plex account by entering a code at plex.tv/link. Mutoscope keeps the sign-in token in this Apple TV's Keychain and uses it to talk to plex.tv and to your Plex Media Servers: to list your servers and libraries, show artwork and details, play media, and save your watch progress and ratings on your server. What Plex does with that information is covered by Plex's own privacy policy (plex.tv/about/privacy-legal). Signing out in Settings → Account removes the token from this Apple TV.

Other services

  • Trakt, only if you link a Trakt account in Settings → Account: Mutoscope reads Trakt's ratings, reviews and comments for what you browse and, if you choose, sends your ratings to your Trakt account. Trakt's privacy policy covers what it keeps. Unlinking removes the Trakt token from this Apple TV.
  • AniList: for anime, Mutoscope asks AniList for public ratings, reviews and discussions, sending only the anime's identifier. No account is involved.
  • Anime-IDs list: Mutoscope downloads Kometa's public list matching anime to AniList from GitHub. No information about you is sent.

What stays on this Apple TV

  • Your settings and profiles.
  • Short preview clips and artwork, cached so they appear quickly. Settings → Browsing can clear the preview cache.
  • In test versions (TestFlight) only, and only if you allow it when the app first opens: a diagnostics log of what the app did, for investigating problems: screens, remote presses and what had focus, the titles and server names you browsed and played, network requests and playback, and a report of each crash. Passwords, tokens and PINs are never recorded. It's kept to a fixed size, older parts are deleted automatically, Settings → Advanced → Clear Diagnostic Logs deletes it, and turning Share Diagnostics off stops it and deletes it. The App Store version keeps no such log.
  • The server list and continue-watching items the Top Shelf shows.

Reporting a review or comment

Holding Select on a Trakt or AniList review or comment lets you report it. When your profile has a linked Trakt account, a Trakt post is reported to Trakt's moderators. Otherwise (AniList's posts, or Trakt's without a linked account) the report goes to the developer: the post's text, author, link and the reason you picked, the title it was on, the app's version and build, the tvOS version and Apple TV model, and the random tag described below. It's stored and handled like a problem report, and nothing from the diagnostics log is sent with it. Reported posts, and the posts of authors you block, are hidden on your profile; Settings → Account → Community can show them again.

What test versions can send the developer

In test versions (TestFlight) with diagnostics allowed, nothing leaves this Apple TV for the developer unless you choose to send it. The App Store version has none of this:

  • Report a Problem (Settings → Advanced, or hold Play/Pause anywhere in the app): sends the kind of problem you picked, what you wrote, a picture of the screen as it was when you asked (video shows black), and the diagnostics log. The panel says what it sends before you press Send.
  • Upload Crash Logs (Settings → Advanced): sends the recent crash reports, the diagnostics log of the sessions they happened in, and the current session.

Either one also sends the app's version and build, the tvOS version and Apple TV model, the language, region and time zone, the app's settings, the identifier this installation of Mutoscope uses with Plex, and a random tag made the first time something is uploaded (it tells uploads from the same Apple TV apart, not who you are). It isn't linked to your Plex account and is never used for advertising or tracking.

Uploads are stored in Google Firebase Cloud Storage. A problem report is also filed as an issue in the developer's private issue tracker on GitHub, and the developer gets a notification about it through Telegram. They are used only to find and fix problems in Mutoscope, are kept only as long as that takes, and are not sold or shared with anyone else.

To have uploads deleted, write to the developer through mutoscope.app, with the Session shown in Settings → Advanced.

Children

Mutoscope isn't directed at children and doesn't knowingly collect information from them.

Changes

If this policy changes, the new version will be in the app and at the link on the App Store page, with its effective date.

Contact

Write to the developer through mutoscope.app.
